HBO built its reputation on storytelling that trusted its audience. The Sopranos, The Wire, Deadwood, Band of Brothers -- these were shows that respected you enough to let you draw your own conclusions. They were morally complex without being morally instructive. That reputation is why HBO commands the loyalty it does. And that reputation is what makes the platform's 2026 output so worth examining.

Our database now holds 38 HBO and Max originals with completed VirtueVigil Woke Scores. The range is staggering: from The Bride! at a -24.0 margin (STRONGLY WOKE) to Chernobyl at a +26.0 margin (STRONGLY TRADITIONAL). That 50-point spread within a single platform is something no other streamer or studio in our database comes close to matching. Netflix clusters woke. Disney clusters woke-lean with carefully managed exceptions. HBO and Max, uniquely, contain multitudes -- and that is both the platform's greatest strength and its most confusing feature for parents trying to navigate it.

The distribution tells a clear story. Two entries land STRONGLY WOKE, four WOKE, and seven WOKE LEAN -- that is 13 progressive-leaning titles. On the other side, six entries land STRONGLY TRADITIONAL and thirteen TRADITIONAL, with five more TRADITIONAL LEAN -- 24 titles that lean traditional or stronger. The middle ground is thin: just three MIXED entries. HBO does not do neutrality. When the platform commits to an ideological direction, it commits fully, and the audience gets to decide which direction they are being pulled.

What stands out most when you look at the data chronologically is the divergence between HBO's original productions and the Warner Bros. film library that fills out Max. HBO originals from 2025-2026 -- The Pitt, Succession, The White Lotus, The Last of Us -- cluster heavily on the woke side. The traditional half of the list is dominated by legacy Warner Bros. films (Casablanca, The Wizard of Oz, The Lord of the Rings, The Dark Knight-adjacent Batman) and a handful of older HBO productions (Chernobyl, True Detective Season 1, Game of Thrones Season 1) that predate the platform's current ideological commitments. The message for parents is straightforward: the HBO original your teenager wants to watch in 2026 is probably pushing an agenda. The classic film in the Max library your parents recommended is probably not. Ranked from most woke to most traditional.

STRONGLY WOKE (Margin -20.0 and Below)

#1: The Bride! (2026)

Woke Score: 34.8 • Traditional Score: 10.4 • Verdict: STRONGLY WOKE • Margin: -24.0

Genre: Gothic Romance / Horror | Platform: Theatrical (IMAX) / HBO Max

Maggie Gyllenhaal's The Bride! reimagines the Bride of Frankenstein as a feminist gothic romance set in 1936 Chicago, with Jessie Buckley playing a murdered woman resurrected by a female scientist (Annette Bening). The Universal monster is repurposed as a vehicle for exploring female autonomy, bodily agency, and the violence inherent in the male gaze. Christian Bale's monster is both threat and sympathetic figure. At 34.8 woke to 10.4 traditional, the margin of -24.0 reflects an ideological project that touches every element of production design, character arc, and thematic resolution. The craft is high. The politics are the product.

#2: The Pitt: Season 2 (2026)

Woke Score: 29.9 • Traditional Score: 9.94 • Verdict: STRONGLY WOKE • Margin: -20.0

Genre: Medical Drama | Platform: HBO Max

The Pitt Season 2 follows the same real-time format as Season 1 -- each episode covers roughly one hour of a single fifteen-hour shift at the Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center -- but the setting shifts to the Fourth of July for maximum dramatic irony. Noah Wyle is exceptional as Dr. Robby, giving one of the most committed performances on television. But the show's ideological architecture is unmistakable: the health care system is broken by design, the patients who suffer most are marginalized, and every institutional failure maps to a political choice. At 29.9 woke to 9.94 traditional, the margin of -20.0 reflects a medical drama that has fully committed to diagnosing America rather than just its patients. The craft is superb. The politics are the prescription.

WOKE (Margin -10.0 to -19.9)

#3: Birds of Prey (2020)

Woke Score: 23.34 • Traditional Score: 5.05 • Verdict: WOKE • Margin: -18.0

Genre: Superhero Action / Dark Comedy | Platform: Theatrical / HBO Max

Birds of Prey (and the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn) is the DCEU's most aggressively female-centric film, built around Margot Robbie's Harley Quinn breaking free from the Joker and assembling an all-female team. The film's aesthetic -- glitter, baseball bats, breakfast sandwiches, chaos -- is deliberately coded as feminine rebellion against male-dominated superhero conventions. Ewan McGregor's Roman Sionis is a cartoon of toxic masculinity. At 23.34 woke to just 5.05 traditional, the margin of -18.0 reflects a film whose ideological project is the entire premise: female solidarity as liberation, male authority as the enemy, and comic-book violence as catharsis. The action sequences have real energy. The politics are front and center.

#4: Succession (Season 1) (2018)

Woke Score: 16.9 • Traditional Score: 2.4 • Verdict: WOKE • Margin: -15.0

Genre: Satirical Comedy-Drama | Platform: HBO / Max | Director: Mark Mylod, Adam McKay, Adam Arkin | Rating: TV-MA

Cast: Brian Cox, Jeremy Strong, Sarah Snook, Kieran Culkin

Succession is frequently mistaken for a conservative show -- rich people behaving badly, patriarchal authority, inherited power -- but the satire's target is unmistakable. The Roys are not celebrated; they are autopsied. Every traditional structure the show depicts -- family loyalty, marriage, inheritance, capitalism itself -- is revealed as hollow, corrupt, and ultimately self-destroying. Brian Cox's Logan Roy is a magnificent monster, but the show's thesis is that the system that produced him is the real villain. At 16.9 woke to just 2.4 traditional, the margin of -15.0 reflects a show that uses the language of prestige drama to deliver a progressive critique that many viewers miss because they are too busy enjoying the insults. The writing is exceptional. The worldview is not neutral.

WOKE LEAN (Margin -2.0 to -9.9)

#5: Dune: Part Two (2024)

Woke Score: 19.36 • Traditional Score: 11.55 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -8.0

Genre: Sci-Fi & Fantasy | Platform: Theatrical / Max

Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part Two completes the adaptation of Frank Herbert's seminal novel with staggering visual ambition and genuine cinematic sweep. The film's ideological complexity lies in how it handles Paul Atreides's ascension: is the messiah figure a hero, a manipulator, or a warning about charismatic leaders who weaponize faith? Zendaya's Chani is elevated from the book's relatively passive role into the film's moral conscience -- a choice that strengthens the film dramatically while shifting its ideological center. At 19.36 woke to 11.55 traditional, the margin of -8.0 reflects a film whose skepticism of religious and political authority aligns with progressive concerns, but whose epic scope and reverence for Herbert's world prevent it from tipping further. The traditional elements are real: honor, sacrifice, destiny as weight rather than escape.

#6: The Last of Us - Season 2 (2026)

Woke Score: 11.0 • Traditional Score: 3.0 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -8.0

Genre: Drama | Platform: HBO

Season 1 earned enormous trust through grounded storytelling and earned emotional beats. Season 2 leverages that trust to introduce ideological reframing that would not have survived scrutiny if presented upfront. What made the first season compelling -- moral complexity, survival-driven choices, earned relationships -- is gradually replaced by identity-driven narrative restructuring. Pedro Pascal and Bella Ramsey remain exceptional performers, and the production values are HBO at its peak. At 11.0 woke to just 3.0 traditional, the gap of 8.0 is smaller than many entries on this list -- but the context matters. This is a franchise that earned conservative viewership and then spent that capital.

#7: The White Lotus: Season 3 (2025)

Woke Score: 19.5 • Traditional Score: 12.8 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -7.0

Genre: Dark Comedy Drama | Platform: HBO / Max

Mike White's third season relocates the wealthy-guest anthology to a Thai wellness resort, swapping Sicilian sexual politics for Eastern spirituality as the object of affluent Western consumption. The formula remains intact -- beautiful people, beautiful location, every character a study in moral failure -- but the critique has sharpened. The show's ideological signature emerges not from any character's politics but from the architecture of the satire itself: wealth is corrosive, privilege is blindness, and every attempt at self-improvement is just another form of consumption. At 19.5 woke to 12.8 traditional, the margin of -7.0 reflects a show that is more interested in anatomizing its characters than preaching at its audience. The traditional 12.8 score comes from genuine consequences and a moral framework that, however bleak, takes behavior seriously.

#8: Blue Beetle (2023)

Woke Score: 15.1 • Traditional Score: 8.8 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -6.0

Genre: Superhero / Action | Platform: Theaters / Max

Blue Beetle is the rare superhero film that earns goodwill through specificity rather than scale. Xolo Mariduena plays Jaime Reyes, a recent college grad who bonds with an alien scarab and becomes a reluctant hero, and the film's best asset is the Reyes family -- warm, funny, interfering, and alive in ways that most superhero supporting casts never achieve. The film is built on a critique of corporate exploitation and military-industrial overreach, with Susan Sarandon's villain as a cartoon of wealthy white indifference. At 15.1 woke to 8.8 traditional, the margin of -6.0 reflects a film whose progressive politics are real but whose investment in family, community, and earned responsibility provides enough traditional weight to keep it from tilting further. The heart is what works here, and heart is not ideological.

#9: The Matrix Resurrections (2021)

Woke Score: 15.1 • Traditional Score: 8.8 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -6.0

Genre: Sci-Fi Action | Platform: Theatrical / HBO Max

Lana Wachowski's return to the Matrix is a film that openly resents having to exist. The first act is essentially a metacommentary on Warner Bros. forcing a sequel, with characters literally debating the meaning of "The Matrix 4" in a writers' room. Keanu Reeves and Carrie-Anne Moss bring genuine warmth to a reuniting of Neo and Trinity that works as romance even as the philosophical machinery around them strains. At 15.1 woke to 8.8 traditional, the margin of -6.0 reflects Wachowski's career-long commitment to trans allegory and anti-establishment themes now filtered through middle-aged exhaustion with the franchise machine. The film is less ideologically aggressive than the originals, but its politics remain the organizing principle of its universe.

#10: Death of a Unicorn (2025)

Woke Score: 16.9 • Traditional Score: 12.3 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -5.0

Genre: Dark Fantasy / Comedy Horror | Platform: Theatrical / HBO Max

Death of a Unicorn arrives with a premise that sounds like it was written by an algorithm trained on A24's marketing department: Jenna Ortega and Paul Rudd play a father and daughter who accidentally hit a unicorn with their car, then discover the pharmaceutical implications of its blood. What follows is a dark comedy about corporate greed, the exploitation of nature, and the impossibility of innocence in a system designed to commodify everything. At 16.9 woke to 12.3 traditional, the margin of -5.0 reflects a film whose critique of capitalism and environmental exploitation is offset by a genuine father-daughter relationship, real moral stakes, and a creature whose magic is treated with actual reverence. The 12.3 traditional score is earned by the film's willingness to take the unicorn seriously, not just as metaphor.

#11: House of the Dragon (Season 3) (2026)

Woke Score: 8.33 • Traditional Score: 5.07 • Verdict: WOKE LEAN • Margin: -3.0

Genre: Fantasy / Drama | Platform: HBO / Max | Rating: TV-MA

Cast: Emma D'Arcy, Matt Smith, Olivia Cooke, Tom Glynn-Carney

Season 3 of House of the Dragon arrives with the Dance of the Dragons fully ignited and the show's ideological commitments fully visible. Rhaenyra Targaryen's arc has evolved from rightful heir denied by patriarchy into a meditation on female leadership under siege -- the men around her undermine, betray, and condescend, and the show frames every setback as structurally determined rather than personally earned. At 8.33 woke to 5.07 traditional, the margin of -3.0 is the narrowest of any woke-leaning entry on this list. The dragon battles are spectacular, Emma D'Arcy remains compelling, and the show's medieval political architecture still provides real traditional counterweight. But the framing has tilted: the Greens are wrong not just politically but morally, and the show is less interested in ambiguity than it was in Season 1.

MIXED (Margin -1.9 to +1.9)

#12: Wonder Woman 1984 (2020)

Woke Score: 18.18 • Traditional Score: 16.3 • Verdict: MIXED • Margin: -2.0

Genre: Superhero Action | Platform: Theatrical / HBO Max

Wonder Woman 1984 is a fascinating ideological artifact because it cannot decide what it wants to be. Gal Gadot's Diana Prince is earnestly heroic in ways that feel genuinely traditional -- she saves people because it is right, not because it is political. But the film surrounds her with 1980s excess-satire, a female villain (Kristen Wiig's Cheetah) whose arc is explicitly about female insecurity exploited by predatory male attention, and a MacGuffin that punishes wish-fulfillment in ways that read as both conservative moralizing and progressive critique of consumer capitalism. At 18.18 woke to 16.3 traditional, the margin of -2.0 makes this the closest to true balance of any HBO/Max entry in our database. The film is messy. It is also, in that messiness, more ideologically honest than most entries on either side of this list.

#13: House of the Dragon (2022)

Woke Score: 12.92 • Traditional Score: 14.54 • Verdict: MIXED • Margin: 2.0

Genre: Fantasy / Epic Drama | Platform: HBO / Max

House of the Dragon's first season pulled off something remarkable in the current television landscape: it told a story about succession, patriarchy, and power in which both sides had a legitimate claim. The show's framing of Rhaenyra as rightful heir denied by gender convention gave it a woke entry point, but its refusal to villainize the Greens entirely -- Alicent's sincere belief, Aemond's genuinely earned grievance -- provided traditional counterweight. At 12.92 woke to 14.54 traditional, the margin of +2.0 makes this a rare MIXED verdict from the traditional side. The show's moral seriousness, willingness to show consequences across generations, and genuine interest in the tragedy of both claimants are what earned those traditional points. This is what ideological complexity looks like when it works.

#14: The Flash (2023)

Woke Score: 9.8 • Traditional Score: 11.48 • Verdict: MIXED • Margin: 2.0

Genre: Superhero / Sci-Fi | Platform: Max

The Flash is a film whose off-screen controversies overshadowed its on-screen content, and the score reflects the product, not the star. Ezra Miller's Barry Allen learns a genuinely conservative lesson -- you cannot fix the past, and trying to do so makes everything worse -- delivered through a multiverse plot that brings back Michael Keaton's Batman as the film's moral center. At 9.8 woke to 11.48 traditional, the margin of +2.0 reflects a film whose core argument about accepting loss and living with consequences is fundamentally traditional, even as the surrounding DCEU machinery carries woke elements. Keaton's Batman is the key: a weary, principled man who kept fighting because it was right, not because it was rewarding. That is not a progressive idea, and the film is better for it.

Woke Score: 5.22 • Traditional Score: 7.43 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL LEAN • Margin: 2.2

Paddy Considine's Viserys Targaryen is the moral anchor of House of the Dragon's first season -- a good man trying to hold his family together while his body fails him, and the show treats his goodness as real rather than naive. The season's ideological signature is more complex than the series as a whole would later become: the succession crisis is driven by genuine ambiguity about duty, oaths, and what a ruler owes their realm. At 5.22 woke to 7.43 traditional, the margin of +2.2 is modest but meaningful. The show's willingness to treat tradition, oath-keeping, and family duty as real moral forces rather than obstacles to be overcome earned those traditional points. Subsequent seasons would drift left. This season holds the line.

#19: The Penguin (2024)

Woke Score: 9.0 • Traditional Score: 14.0 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL LEAN • Margin: 5.0

Genre: Crime Drama | Platform: HBO

Colin Farrell disappears so completely into Oswald Cobblepot that you forget you are watching a man in prosthetics within five minutes of the first episode. The Penguin is a gangster story in the classic HBO mold -- ambitious, violent, morally compromised, and completely uninterested in making its protagonist sympathetic. At 9.0 woke to 14.0 traditional, the margin of +5.0 reflects a show whose traditional elements are baked into the genre: a man clawing his way up a criminal hierarchy through violence and cunning, with consequences that compound rather than resolve. The show's refusal to frame Cobblepot as a victim of the system -- he is the system's predator, and he knows it -- is what keeps the woke score in single digits. This is HBO doing what HBO used to do: trusting the audience to watch a bad man without needing a lecture about why he is bad.

TRADITIONAL (Margin +8.0 to +19.9)

#20: Juror #2 (2024)

Woke Score: 5.95 • Traditional Score: 15.54 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL • Margin: 10.0

Genre: Crime / Drama / Mystery | Platform: Theatrical / Max | Director: Clint Eastwood | Distributor: Warner Bros. | Rating: PG-13

Cast: Nicholas Hoult, Toni Collette, J.K. Simmons, Zoey Deutch

Clint Eastwood, at 94, directed a courtroom drama about a man who realizes during jury selection that he may be the one who committed the crime. Nicholas Hoult plays Justin Kemp, a recovering alcoholic whose past threatens to consume his present, and the film's moral architecture is pure Eastwood: individual conscience versus institutional machinery, personal responsibility as the only path to redemption, and a justice system that cannot deliver what only the human heart can. At 5.95 woke to 15.54 traditional, the margin of +10.0 reflects a filmmaker who has spent six decades making movies about what it means to be morally serious. The craft is quiet. The argument is devastating.

#21: The Boy and the Heron (2023)

Woke Score: 3.6 • Traditional Score: 14.7 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL • Margin: 11.0

Genre: Animated Fantasy Drama | Platform: Theatrical / Max

Hayao Miyazaki's supposed final film is a meditation on grief, legacy, and the weight of inheritance -- themes that Miyazaki has explored his entire career but here renders with the clarity of an artist who knows he is approaching the end. The story follows Mahito, a boy who loses his mother in a Tokyo firebombing and enters a fantastical world that is part escape, part reckoning. At just 3.6 woke to 14.7 traditional, the margin of +11.0 reflects a film whose moral universe is built on personal responsibility, the obligation to carry forward what came before, and the understanding that fantasy is not an escape from the real world but a way of preparing to re-enter it. No contemporary American studio would make this film. That is the point.

#22: Good Will Hunting (1997)

Woke Score: 6.8 • Traditional Score: 18.2 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL • Margin: 11.0

Genre: Drama | Platform: Theatrical (Miramax) / Max

Matt Damon and Ben Affleck's breakthrough script remains one of the most emotionally coherent films about male vulnerability, mentorship, and the courage it takes to accept love ever made in America. Will Hunting is a math genius working as a janitor at MIT, and the film's argument is not that the system failed him -- it is that he is failing himself by refusing to risk the vulnerability that genuine connection requires. At 6.8 woke to 18.2 traditional, the margin of +11.0 reflects a film whose entire moral architecture is built on the belief that people need each other, that running from commitment is cowardice, and that the best thing one man can do for another is to tell him the truth. Robin Williams's Sean Maguire is the finest on-screen therapist in American cinema because he believes in Will's soul, not his potential.

#23: Shazam! Fury of the Gods (2023)

Woke Score: 5.9 • Traditional Score: 17.5 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL • Margin: 12.0

Genre: Superhero / Action | Platform: Max

Shazam! Fury of the Gods is the kind of superhero sequel nobody expected to score this traditionally. Zachary Levi's Billy Batson is still a kid in a superhero's body, and the film's central concern is the foster family he is terrified of losing -- not as metaphor, but as literal, specific, earned relationships. At 5.9 woke to 17.5 traditional, the margin of +12.0 reflects a film whose commitment to family, loyalty, and self-sacrifice as genuine goods rather than coded politics gives it one of the strongest traditional scores in the superhero genre. The mythology is silly. The heart is not. The final act's faith in the power of family to overcome literal gods is the kind of thing Hollywood used to know how to do in its sleep and now mostly fumbles.

#24: Dune: Part One (2021)

Woke Score: 7.1 • Traditional Score: 20.02 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL • Margin: 13.0

Genre: Sci-Fi Epic | Platform: Theaters / HBO Max

Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part One is a film about a young man inheriting a destiny he did not choose and learning to bear its weight. The Atreides family is depicted as genuinely noble -- not in the sarcastic modern sense, but in the classical sense of people who take their obligations seriously because those obligations define who they are. At 7.1 woke to 20.02 traditional, the margin of +13.0 reflects a film whose reverence for Frank Herbert's world extends to its moral framework: honor matters, family is sacred, and the difference between a ruler and a tyrant is whether they serve their people or themselves. Oscar Isaac's Duke Leto is the film's moral exemplar -- a man who knows he is walking into a trap and goes anyway because his duty requires it. That is not a progressive idea. It is an ancient one, and Villeneuve treats it with the gravity it deserves.

#25: The Batman (2022)

Woke Score: 8.0 • Traditional Score: 22.1 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL • Margin: 14.0

Genre: Superhero / Crime / Neo-Noir | Platform: Theatrical / Max | Director: Matt Reeves | Distributor: Warner Bros. | Rating: PG-13

Cast: Robert Pattinson, Zoe Kravitz, Paul Dano, Jeffrey Wright

Matt Reeves's The Batman is a detective story first and a superhero movie second, and that choice is what earns it one of the strongest traditional scores on this list. Robert Pattinson's Bruce Wayne is not a playboy or a symbol -- he is a traumatized man who has made violence his religion and is slowly realizing that vengeance is not the same thing as justice. At 8.0 woke to 22.1 traditional, the margin of +14.0 reflects a film whose moral architecture is built on the distinction between revenge and law, chaos and order, despair and hope. Paul Dano's Riddler is a domestic terrorist radicalized online -- a contemporary concern -- but the film's answer is not systemic reform; it is individual courage, institutional persistence, and the recognition that being a symbol of hope is harder and more necessary than being a symbol of fear. That is a fundamentally conservative insight, and Reeves earns it through craft rather than sermon.

#26: The Deer Hunter (1978)

Woke Score: 7.14 • Traditional Score: 21.0 • Verdict: TRADITIONAL • Margin: 14.0

Genre: Drama / War | Platform: Various / Max | Director: Michael Cimino | Distributor: Universal | Rating: R

Cast: Robert De Niro, Christopher Walken, John Savage, Meryl Streep

The Deer Hunter is one of the most devastating films ever made about what war does to the men who fight it, and it earns its traditional score through its understanding that the bonds those men share are sacred precisely because they are tested to destruction. The film's famous Russian roulette sequences are not exploitation -- they are metaphor made literal, the randomness of survival rendered as a game with no strategy except endurance. At 7.14 woke to 21.0 traditional, the margin of +14.0 reflects a film whose entire moral universe is built on male friendship, ethnic community, patriotic obligation, and the impossibility of returning home unchanged. De Niro's Michael is the man who holds it together while his friends fall apart, and the film treats that burden as heroic. Fifty years of filmmaking have not produced a more honest portrait of what men owe each other.

#30: The Rock (1996)

Michael Bay's The Rock is the best action movie of the 1990s, and it earns its 2.1 woke score through ideological purity of a particular kind: this is a film about a chemical weapons specialist and a former SAS operative breaking into Alcatraz to stop a rogue general from launching nerve gas at San Francisco. There is no subtext. There is only Sean Connery telling Nicolas Cage that losers always whine about their best while winners go home and make certain promises to the prom queen. Ed Harris's General Hummel is the film's secret weapon -- a villain who is right about the military abandoning his men, and wrong about what to do about it. At 20.02 traditional, the margin of +18.0 reflects a film that believes in duty, sacrifice, and the proposition that Nicolas Cage should be allowed to save America with a VX gas antidote injected directly into his heart.

Game of Thrones Season 1 achieved a waking nightmare for progressive television critics: it made patriarchy look compelling. Sean Bean's Ned Stark is not a critique of masculine honor -- he is its embodiment, and the show treats his death not as a lesson about the failure of traditional values but as a tragedy about what happens when an honorable man enters a dishonorable world. At just 1.0 woke to 20.3 traditional, the margin of +19.0 reflects a season whose moral framework is built on oath, lineage, duty, and the terrible cost of keeping faith in a world that rewards betrayal. The Stark family values are not coded as conservative or progressive -- they are coded as Northern, which in George R.R. Martin's world means old, cold, and the only thing worth dying for. The show would drift significantly in later seasons. This season is a monument to what HBO could do when it trusted its material.

#34: Casablanca (1942)

Casablanca is the greatest argument for traditional values ever captured on film, and it makes that argument without once raising its voice. Rick Blaine is a man who has withdrawn from the world because the world broke his heart, and the film's entire dramatic engine is his slow, painful return to moral engagement -- not because anyone lectures him, but because the woman he loves and the cause she represents demand it. At just 0.7 woke to 23.52 traditional, the margin of +23.0 reflects a film whose moral universe is built on sacrifice, duty, and the recognition that some things matter more than personal happiness. "The problems of three little people don't amount to a hill of beans in this crazy world" is not a cynical line. It is the moment Rick chooses the world over himself, and the film treats that choice as heroism. Eighty-four years later, nothing has surpassed it.

At just 0.7 woke to 23.94 traditional, the margin of +23.0 reflects a film that believes in sacrifice, in duty as obligation rather than burden, and in the idea that being a hero means giving up what you want for what other people need. Tobey Maguire's Peter Parker is a dork who gets bullied, and the film does not frame that as systemic injustice -- it frames it as the ordinary cruelty of high school, which he must transcend rather than resent. The upside-down kiss is iconic. The moral framework is why it still works.

#38: Chernobyl (2019)

Woke Score: 2.0 • Traditional Score: 27.72 • Verdict: STRONGLY TRADITIONAL • Margin: 26.0

Genre: Historical Drama | Platform: HBO / Max | Director: Johan Renck | Rating: TV-MA

Cast: Jared Harris, Stellan Skarsgard, Emily Watson, Paul Ritter

Chernobyl is the most traditionally-scored entry in the entire HBO and Max catalog, and the highest traditional score of any television production in our database. This is not an accident. Craig Mazin's five-episode masterpiece is about what happens when a state built on ideology refuses to acknowledge reality, and the answer is: people die. Jared Harris's Valery Legasov is the scientist who must navigate a bureaucracy that punishes truth-telling, and his arc is not a celebration of institutional reform -- it is a testament to the courage of individuals who tell the truth when the system demands lies. At 2.0 woke to 27.72 traditional, the margin of +26.0 reflects a show whose moral framework is built on truth, sacrifice, and the recognition that some things -- radiation, reality, human courage -- do not respond to ideology. The final episode's courtroom scene, in which Legasov explains exactly how and why the reactor exploded, is the most devastating refutation of ideological thinking ever broadcast on American television. HBO will almost certainly never make anything like it again. That is the tragedy.

The Takeaway

HBO and Max present a platform of ideological extremes. Two STRONGLY WOKE entries at the top, six STRONGLY TRADITIONAL entries at the bottom, and a 50-point margin spread that no other streamer or studio in our database comes close to matching. The shape of the distribution matters: 13 titles lean woke or stronger, 24 lean traditional or stronger, and just 3 land in the MIXED middle. HBO does not do neutrality.

The split between HBO originals and the Warner Bros. film library is the most important pattern in the data. HBO's 2025-2026 original productions -- The Pitt, Succession, The Last of Us, The White Lotus -- cluster heavily on the woke side. The traditional half of the list is dominated by legacy films (Casablanca, The Wizard of Oz, The Lord of the Rings) and older HBO productions (Chernobyl, True Detective Season 1, Game of Thrones Season 1) that predate the platform's current ideological commitments. Parents navigating Max for family viewing should understand: the HBO original your teenager wants to watch in 2026 is probably pushing an agenda. The classic film in the library your parents recommended is probably not.

The Pitt is the most instructive case study on this list. Season 1, released in 2025, earned a +17.0 margin -- solidly TRADITIONAL, built on medical competence and the moral weight of life-and-death decisions. Season 2, released in 2026, flipped to a -20.0 margin -- STRONGLY WOKE, with the show diagnosing America rather than its patients. That 37-point swing within a single calendar year is not a creative evolution. It is an ideological pivot, and audiences who trusted the show after Season 1 deserve to know what changed.

The traditional titans at the bottom of this list deserve particular attention. Chernobyl at +26.0, The Two Towers at +25.0, The Wizard of Oz at +24.0 -- these are not marginal results. They reflect films and shows whose moral frameworks are so thoroughly traditional that they are essentially immune to progressive reinterpretation. Chernobyl's argument -- that ideology kills, and truth is the only defense -- is the most explicitly anti-progressive statement in prestige television. The Two Towers' argument -- that there is good in this world worth fighting for -- is the kind of thing you cannot say in a writers' room in 2026 without someone asking you to define "good." These are not reactionary works. They are works that predate the current ideological dispensation entirely, and they endure because their moral seriousness transcends the moment they were made in.

The question for HBO and Max going forward is whether the platform recognizes what its own catalog is telling it. The traditional half of this list represents some of the most beloved and enduring content in the history of the medium. The woke half represents content that, in many cases, will struggle to be remembered five years from now. The data is clear. Whether the platform processes it is another question entirely.
